about: Strikes and planned disruptions affecting travellers in Portugal, 17 November to 31 December 2026, Algarve first, with 1 to 16 November 2026 as context. Standard line for every item: Your airline or operator decides whether your service runs: its site or app has the latest. Only items confirmed by at least one named publisher are listed; the rest are in gaps.

items.title: easyJet cabin crew strike of 19 to 23 December: called off
items.where: easyJet bases at Lisbon, Porto and Faro
items.what: The cabin crew union SNPVAC called off the five-day strike it had called for 19 to 23 December at easyJet's Lisbon, Porto and Faro bases. It did so on 18 November, after easyJet made a proposal in conciliation at DGERT. The union says this is a starting point for talks, not an agreement, and that it could call new action if the talks stall; meetings are set for 20, 23 and 25 November. No report of the 20 November meeting found by 19:55 UTC on 20 November. Flights on those dates should run as normal, but check with easyJet before you travel.

items.title: easyJet cabin crew strike of 2 to 6 October (context)
items.where: easyJet bases at Lisbon, Porto and Faro
items.what: The union said 370 flights were cancelled over the five days, most of them before the strike began. The airline said it had planned 786 flights and cut to 442. Figures are the union's and the airline's own. Background for the December dates.

items.title: Storm Charles: flight cancellations and road closures on 11 November
items.where: Mainland Portugal including the Algarve; Lisbon, Porto, Faro and Madeira airports
items.what: The government declared a state of alert for 11 November. ANA reported close to 400 cancelled flights across Lisbon, Porto, Faro and Madeira, counting earlier cancellations. Civil Protection logged 76 incidents in the Algarve by 14:00 with roads closed or restricted in four municipalities. The Algarve red weather warning was lifted in the afternoon. The prime minister said the impact was smaller than forecast. No lingering travel effect was found for the days since. Your airline or operator decides whether your service runs: its site or app has the latest.

items.title: EU Entry/Exit System: biometric checks and arrival queues at Portuguese airports, Faro under most pressure
items.where: Faro, Lisbon and Porto airports; Faro named as under greater pressure
items.what: Biometric collection for non-EU arrivals became mandatory on 6 September. As of 13 September the PSP said Faro was under the most pressure, with many flights, often carrying British passengers, landing close together. The PSP said it can skip biometrics during technical problems, which the Commission allows until December. Lisbon waits were given as 15 to 30 minutes. No November waiting-time figures were found. This is an ongoing situation, not a dated event.
